name: Platform Conventions Rulebook
summary: Principles from Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and Microsoft Fluent 2, applied to the web.
check: Change OS settings (dark mode, reduced motion, larger text, more contrast) and reload.

rules.title: Purpose first
rules.text: Know what the product is for and make those few things great before adding anything else. Every element earns its place; simplicity is not the same as minimalism.

rules.title: Agency
rules.text: Let people move freely, skip guided flows, and recover from mistakes. Forgiveness (undo, back, drafts) makes people confident to explore (`IX-15`).

rules.title: Familiarity
rules.text: Build on patterns people know from the web and their OS. Familiar controls in the expected place beat clever new ones (`IX-02`).

rules.title: Responsibility
rules.text: Be transparent about what the product does with data, ask for permissions with a reason at the moment they are needed, collect only what is needed (`SEC-17`).

rules.title: Delight is not decoration
rules.text: Delight comes from the sum of care: speed, clear feedback, kind words in errors, one well-made moment. Effects that slow the task are not delight.

rules.title: Respect user settings
rules.text: Colour scheme, reduced motion, reduced transparency, more contrast, text size and language preferences of the browser and OS are honoured, not overridden.

rules.title: Materials only in the control layer
rules.text: Translucent "glass" belongs to bars and overlays that float over content (a header over a photo, a sheet over a map), never to content cards, and never stacked glass on glass. Text on glass uses a thicker material or a scrim (`SL-04`).

rules.title: Concentric corners
rules.text: Nested radii follow the parent: inner radius = outer radius − padding (`DC-14`). Radii come from a small radius scale.

rules.title: Elevation by meaning
rules.text: A small elevation ramp (for example rest, raised, popover, dialog) where higher means more temporary and more important. Shadows are soft, low and few (`SL-05`, `SL-53`).

rules.title: Platform-appropriate input
rules.text: Hover and right-click on desktop, large targets and thumb reach on phones, visible focus for keyboard, and voice/screen-reader-friendly labels.

rules.title: Same experience across sizes
rules.text: Content and controls keep predictable positions when the window resizes; layouts change structure (tab bar to sidebar), not function (`LY-14`).

rules.title: Native app look on the web only when it is an app
rules.text: A web app may borrow platform patterns (sidebar, toolbar, segmented controls); a marketing site should not dress up as an operating system.

rules.title: Respect the reading direction
rules.text: Use logical CSS properties (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`) so layouts mirror correctly for right-to-left languages.

rules.title: Breaking the back button
rules.text: Navigation, filters and opened items create history entries where people expect them, and Back always returns to the previous view.
